title: Biodiversity and the effect of human interaction
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.7.3-c09 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.7.3-c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.7.3-c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.7.3-c05 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.7.3-q01, 4.7.3-q03, 4.7.3-q04, 4.7.3-q06, 4.7.3-q07, 4.7.3-q08, 4.7.3-q02, 4.7.3-q05.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Large-scale deforestation
items.clue: Clearing tropical woodland for cattle, rice fields or biofuel crops.

items.label: Biodiversity
items.clue: The variety of all the different species in an ecosystem or on Earth.

items.label: Global warming
items.clue: The rise in average temperature linked to more carbon dioxide and methane in the air.

items.label: Pollution
items.clue: Harmful substances released into water, air or land, such as sewage, smoke or toxic chemicals.

questions.stem: What is meant by the biodiversity of an ecosystem?

options.text: The total number of individual organisms there
Number of different habitats found in the area
The number of species that depend on one another
The variety of the different species living there

questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of all the different species of organisms on earth, or within an ecosystem.

questions.stem: As the human population grows, more untreated sewage and fertiliser drain into a river and many fish and plants die. What is the effect on the river?

options.text: There is no pollution as both are natural materials
Pollution kills organisms and biodiversity falls
Biodiversity is unchanged as fish numbers recover
Biodiversity falls but the ecosystem becomes stable

questions.explanation: More waste is produced as the population grows, and unless it is properly handled more pollution is caused; pollution kills plants and animals which can reduce biodiversity.

questions.stem: Part of an area of grassland is quarried for stone and the rest is ploughed to grow crops. What is the effect on other animals and plants?

options.text: Less land is available for other plants and animals
Quarrying reduces the land but farming does not
Biodiversity is unchanged as many individuals stay
The ecosystem is more stable once species are lost

questions.explanation: Humans reduce the amount of land available for other animals and plants by building, quarrying, farming and dumping waste, which reduces biodiversity.

questions.stem: A large area of tropical forest is cleared to grow crops for biofuels. What is the impact on biodiversity?

options.text: Biodiversity is unchanged because biofuels are renewable
Biodiversity falls when the cleared trees are burned
Biodiversity falls as the forest habitat is destroyed
Biodiversity falls, so the ecosystem becomes more stable

questions.explanation: Large-scale deforestation in tropical areas, including clearance to grow crops for biofuels, removes the habitat and so reduces the variety of species living there.

questions.stem: Levels of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere are increasing. Which is a biological consequence of the global warming this causes?

options.text: Species die out where the air becomes much warmer
Some species change the areas where they are found
Areas near carbon dioxide sources are affected most
Ecosystems become more stable as species are lost

questions.explanation: Biological consequences of global warming include loss of habitat, changes in the distribution of species and changes in migration patterns.

questions.stem: A government wants to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity. Which policy would have a positive impact?

options.text: Growing more crops that will be used to make biofuels
Spreading extra fertiliser on farmland each season
Digging up more peat bogs to sell as garden compost
Reducing deforestation and carbon dioxide emissions

questions.explanation: Reduction of deforestation and of carbon dioxide emissions by some governments is one of the programmes put in place to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.stem: A woodland has a great biodiversity. Why is this ecosystem more stable?

options.text: The number of individual organisms stays the same
Each species depends more on others for shelter
One species depends less on others for its food
The area contains a larger number of habitats

questions.explanation: A great biodiversity ensures the stability of ecosystems by reducing the dependence of one species on another for food, shelter and the maintenance of the physical environment.

questions.stem: A peat bog is drained and the peat is dug out and sold as garden compost. What are the effects?

options.text: The habitat is lost and carbon dioxide is released
Carbon dioxide is released by burning, not by decay
Biodiversity is unchanged as many organisms survive
The land stays available because it is not built on

questions.explanation: The destruction of peat bogs to produce garden compost reduces the area of this habitat, and thus its biodiversity, and the decay or burning of the peat releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
